differences.title: 1. CONFIG MODEL
differences.leftDesc: Caddy uses a Caddyfile with opinionated directives that compile into an internal config graph. Common tasks (TLS, redirects, reverse_proxy) stay declarative and order-safe for typical HTTP reverse-proxy setups.
differences.rightDesc: HAProxy relies on explicit, low-level directives (frontends/backends, ACLs, rules) that map directly to runtime objects. You manually control routing decisions and traffic-flow sequencing across request/response phases.

differences.title: 2. TLS AUTOMATION
differences.leftDesc: Caddy can automatically obtain and renew certificates via ACME, provisioning TLS assets without extra scaffolding. It also supports multiple certificate sources and can hot-reload TLS state efficiently.
differences.rightDesc: HAProxy generally expects you to configure certificates and verification behavior explicitly in its TLS bind lines. While it can integrate with external automation, HAProxy itself focuses on fast forwarding and precise TLS policy.

differences.title: 3. PROXYING ENGINE
differences.leftDesc: Caddy’s reverse_proxy is built around HTTP handling primitives: it terminates connections, applies HTTP middleware, then streams to upstreams while preserving headers and managing timeouts per-route.
differences.rightDesc: HAProxy uses an event-driven architecture with highly optimized I/O loops. It can handle large numbers of concurrent connections with minimal overhead and supports both HTTP and raw TCP proxying.

differences.title: 4. LOAD BALANCING STRATEGIES
differences.leftDesc: Caddy’s upstream selection is typically configured with straightforward policies and health checks, aiming for quick deployment. It’s great for common round-robin/least-latency style needs with clear configuration.
differences.rightDesc: HAProxy provides a wide set of proven load balancing methods and stickiness options, including consistent hashing and fine-grained health checks. It also supports per-backend tuning for retries, redispatch, and circuit behaviors.

differences.title: 5. MIDDLEWARE / HTTP FEATURES
differences.leftDesc: Caddy composes HTTP capabilities via middleware-style modules (e.g., auth, headers, rate limiting) around the reverse_proxy handler, enabling clean request/response transformations without spreading logic everywhere.
differences.rightDesc: HAProxy expresses HTTP behavior using rules, ACLs, and message processing stages (request/response). Complex transformations often involve fetch methods and conditional actions, which can be extremely powerful but more verbose.

differences.title: 6. OBSERVABILITY & STATS
differences.leftDesc: Caddy commonly exposes metrics and structured logs through built-in integrations. Its runtime is designed to reload config smoothly, so observability stays consistent across deployments.
differences.rightDesc: HAProxy offers mature operational tooling: an HTTP stats page, runtime socket controls, and detailed per-proxy counters. You can inspect sessions, queues, and errors while tuning without full restarts.

differences.title: 7. BEST-FIT DEPLOYMENT USE CASES
differences.leftDesc: Caddy shines as an edge reverse proxy where frictionless HTTPS and fast iteration matter. Its succinct configuration and automatic certificates reduce operational overhead for many web workloads.
differences.rightDesc: HAProxy excels when you need a central, high-scale load balancing tier with deep routing logic, multi-protocol support, and battle-tested performance characteristics for very large connection volumes.
